meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified continental system) applicable in Mainland China, with Taiwan maintaining a separate civil law system as a sub-region; PRC foreign investment and company law governs WFOE formation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan Investor (Company Registration Certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration and Administration Division
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan-origin instruments use the exclusive Cross-Strait Document Verification path: (1) Taiwan district court notary notarization; (2) Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification and forwarding; (3) mainland notarial association confirmation through ARATS; (4) certified Chinese translation. This path is parallel to and mutually exclusive of the Hague Apostille and consular legalization systems; no apostille and no consular legalization is used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Taiwan equivalent Certificate of Company Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration and Administration Division
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait verification only: Taiwan notary public notarization, SEF verification, ARATS-linked mainland notarial association confirmation, and Chinese translation. Not subject to Hague Apostille or PRC consular legalization because Taiwan has no apostille authority and no PRC embassy in Taiwan.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the WFOE formation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Taiwan investor, notarized by a Taiwan district notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait verification only: Taiwan notary public notarization of board signatures, SEF verification, mainland notarial association confirmation through ARATS, and Chinese translation. Apostille and consular legalization are not applicable and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (certified copy) of the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (company registry certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait verification only: notarization by Taiwan notary public, SEF verification, mainland notarial association confirmation via ARATS, and certified Chinese translation. This is the sole authentication route; neither Hague Apostille nor consular legalization applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the Taiwan investor's bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank in Taiwan under bank seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait verification only: bank letter executed before a Taiwan notary public, SEF verification, mainland notarial association confirmation, and Chinese translation. No apostille and no consular legalization route is available or required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Business Scope and Industry Classification (to support the digital publishing scope)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Cross-Strait verification only: Taiwan notary public notarization, SEF verification and forwarding, mainland notarial association verification through ARATS, and Chinese translation; parallel and exclusive relative to Hague Apostille and consular legalization paths.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover each UBO, director, senior manager and authorized signatory, including Taiwanese principals, against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, China's List of Unreliable Entities, PRC terrorist financing designations, and Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission sanctions. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by politically exposed persons (PEPs) holding any ownership, control, or beneficial interest, regardless of the 25% threshold. A two-level negative news and adverse media search, a source-of-wealth review for the digital magazine advertising revenue, and a beneficial ownership chain map through all intermediate holding entities must be completed and documented within 24 hours prior to KYC acceptance; screening must be repeated immediately before any Stripe or AdSense payout integration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Independent Declaration System operated by SAMR through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and provincial/municipal one-stop market regulation online platforms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory Chinese company name must use simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier structure: administrative division + trade name (字号) + industry or business characteristic + company type. For the WFOE the company type must be 有限责任公司 or 有限公司. A foreign-language brand may be phonetically transliterated into Chinese and registered as the trade name, but the Chinese name is the exclusive legal name for tax, customs, banking and regulatory filings. Pure English names or names containing only Latin letters are not accepted as the registered company name. The industry segment should include digital publishing or media wording such as 数字传媒 or 互联网出版, consistent with ISIC 5813 and NAICS 511120 activities.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR name declaration system rejects the proposed name, the applicant must file a written administrative reconsideration request with the market regulation authority one administrative level above the rejecting bureau (e.g., from a district bureau to the municipal SAMR) within 60 days of the rejection notice, attaching the proposed four-tier name, the rejection code, and the legal basis for entitlement. The authority must issue a written decision within 30 days. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within 6 months. For collisions with an existing registered name, a separate name-dispute complaint may be submitted, with evidence of prior use, trademark registration or investment contract, seeking revocation of the conflicting name and re-registration of the cleared name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by Chinese tax authorities and commercial banks for a digital magazine portal generating cross-border advertising revenue. The State Taxation Administration and local tax bureaus require a physical office address for issuance of VAT invoices, receipt of tax inspection notices, and on-site audit access; banks conducting account-opening KYC require a physical site visit and verification of signage and personnel. In designated free-trade zones and cluster-registration pilot areas, a government-approved cluster address may be accepted for the business license, but a physical workspace with at least one desk, company signage, records, and employee presence must remain available for unannounced inspections and for the bank's operational substance review. Purely virtual addresses without any physical presence are operationally non-viable for the required payment rails (Stripe and AdSense payouts).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (1) exact registered address and suite number must match the lease and license; (2) company name signage must be displayed at the entrance; (3) lease or ownership documents, property tax receipts, and floor plan must be available; (4) payroll, employment contracts and attendance records must correspond to claimed staff; (5) VAT invoices, accounting books and bank statements must be accessible at the address or via quick electronic production; (6) the company seal must be traceable to the licensed engraver and the registered address. Quantified risk of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months: high (55-70%) for a digital media entity with cross-border advertising revenue and Stripe/AdSense payouts, particularly if registered at a residential or virtual address; moderate (20-30%) for free-trade-zone cluster registration with full compliance and professional third-party records; low (5-10%) for a standard Grade-A office with active staff and complete books.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for a single WFOE formation with Taiwan-source investor, USD 3,000 - 5,000 depending on complexity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate RMB 300 - 500 per page for legal corporate documents, estimated 8 - 12 pages.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR company name pre-reservation and business license issuance

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of Taiwan (公司法), Article 6 (Company Registration), Article 7 (Verification by Central Authority), Article 8 (Responsible Persons), Article 12 (Effect and Alteration of Registration), Article 101 (Limited Company Capital), and Article 128 (Statutory Directors); Foreign Investment Act (外國投資條例), Articles 3 and 10; Ministry of Economic Affairs Organization Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署), with Investment Commission (投資審議司) approval for foreign-owned shareholding.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (公司登記申請書) together with Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), within-twenty-days registration affidavit, board-seat acceptance letters, supervisor consent, CPA capital verification report, and Foreign Investment Commission approval certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a Taiwan limited liability company. The registered capital must be fully subscribed and paid into a dedicated Taiwan bank account before filing, and a certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report confirming deposit balances. No escrow account or blocked funds mandate applies unless imposed as a special condition by the Investment Commission in connection with the foreign ownership approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company CN_WFOE_LTD was duly established under the Companies Act of Taiwan and that all subscribers of record, being the sole shareholder and the founding management nominees, have subscribed for and agreed to take one hundred percent (100%) of the issued ordinary shares for an aggregate paid-in consideration to be maintained in the Company's dedicated registered capital account at a licensed bank in Taiwan. Forthwith, the Chief Financial Officer and the individual authorized as general manager shall deposit all subscribed capital, furnish the certified public accountant's capital verification certificate, and cause the Company registration to be submitted to the Department of Commerce through the centralized online filing system. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be fixed, and the Company is authorized to execute a lease agreement for that office, and all notices, process, and regulatory correspondence may be served at that address. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Bank of Taiwan or another authorized commercial bank is appointed as the Company's principal depository institution. The chairperson, the chief financial officer, and the general manager are individually authorized to open, maintain, sign, close, or pledge transaction accounts, to execute all signature cards, internet banking mandates, wire transfer authorizations, trade finance instruments, and account documentation, and to negotiate checks and receive payments; all such acts being effective upon any two of the authorized officers executing together. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the shareholders and directors do approve the appointment of the following statutory officers for the mandatory positions required by Article 108 of the Companies Act, namely a sole or multiple directors and a supervisor, each of whom has accepted in writing, and that the general manager and company secretary are vested with full authority to execute all employment contracts, licensing applications, procurement orders, publication platform agreements, and payment processor mandates necessary for the digital magazine and sponsored media content business. THIS RESOLUTION is effective as of the date unanimously adopted by the Board of Directors and shall remain in full force and effect until rescinded; all acts performed in reliance hereon are hereby ratified and confirmed in all respects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Legal Capacity Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (線上投資審議系統)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a foreign-invested wholly foreign-owned enterprise using the online Taiwan Investment Commission portal. The filing must set forth the exact identity and tax status of the foreign shareholder, the intended registered capital in New Taiwan Dollars, the proposed corporate name and business scope, and a calendar of the digital magazine portal operations. The protocol requires notarization of the shareholder's certificate of incorporation or equivalent identity document by a Taiwan notary or the Taiwan overseas representative office. All documents must be translated into Traditional Chinese where issued in another language, and translations must be certified. The applicant must pay the application fee at the Taiwan Postal Office or through the portal, and must upload a formalized power of attorney authorizing a local legal representative to complete follow-up submissions.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor certificate of incorporation or ID
Certified English-to-Traditional-Chinese translation
Power of attorney for Taiwanese filing agent
Proposed Articles of Incorporation (final draft)
Business plan and capital deployment schedule
Digital magazine revenue model description and AML low-risk self-declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query, remedy by filing a supplementary explanation and corrected dossiers within fourteen calendar days. If the application is suspended due to incomplete foreign-source documentation, the legal representative may request a formal cure notice listing missing items and submit notarized copies through the same online portal to reactivate review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Statutory Articles Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce Central Registration Database (公司及商業一站式線上申請系統)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After securing investment approval, apply for company name and business scope pre-approval through the Department of Commerce one-stop portal. The proposed Chinese and English names must comply with the Rules on Naming of Company and Business, and the digital magazine scope must match ISIC 5813 under the Taiwan Standard Classification, using the Ministry of Economic Affairs industrial category I301010 for digital publication. Upon pre-approval, the Articles of Incorporation must be prepared with the exact capital amount, the rights and obligations of shares, the number and duties of statutory directors and supervisor, the registered office address, the duration, and the distribution standard. The founding shareholder must sign the articles in person or by validated power of attorney before a notary. The final articles must be uploaded to the Department of Commerce system, and the statutory filing fee of approximately one thousand New Taiwan Dollars must be generated and paid online.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval certificate
Name pre-approval receipt
Notarized or certified Articles of Incorporation
List of directors and supervisor with written acceptance
Identification of statutory officers with domicile proofs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name pre-approval is rejected for duplication, the applicant may submit up to three alternate name candidates within seven days and request a fresh pre-approval. If the notary identifies a capital or articles defect, the shareholder must amend and re-notarize the articles before the Department of Commerce will continue the batch application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Verification and Company Registration Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce and Licensed Taiwanese Certified Public Accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporation bank account is opened and subscribed capital is deposited, a Taiwanese CPA must complete a capital verification audit reviewing deposit slip, bank certificate, shareholder payment proof, and the cash flow. The CPA issues a capital verification report in Traditional Chinese. Thereafter, the full company registration application is submitted online via the Company Registration and One-Stop Service portal. The application must include the articles, all officer acceptance documents, a statement that the company has not yet engaged in any prohibited activity, the capital verification report, the registered office lease or ownership consent, and the Investment Commission approval certificate. The Department of Commerce examines the application for legal compliance, triggers civil-tax integration notifications, and upon approval grants the company registration certificate showing the legal personality of CN_WFOE_LTD.
required_dossiers: CPA capital verification report
Bank deposit certificate and statement ledger
Registration application form
Registered office lease or title document
Investment Commission foreign investment final certificate
Articles and all pertinent resolutions of the board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If application is queried, the responsible legal representative must respond within fifteen days by uploading corrective docs. If registration is suspended for a minor defect such as lease-prefix mismatch, the Department will issue a numbered defect notice; the applicant must cure all items and re-pay the resubmission fee only if the defect notice so states.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Seal Carving, and Post-Incorporation Bank Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan (工商登記及稅籍登記)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the company registration certificate, the company must complete tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau through the national integrated filing system. The digital magazine company must be registered for Business Tax (VAT) if expected annual revenue exceeds the threshold, and must apply for a unified invoice serial number. The chairman, in person, must then register the company official seal and the responsible person seal with the local company registry, following the seal-carving protocol, and submit the official seal specimen to the bank to activate the capital account for operational use. The company secretary shall file all post-incorporation conditions from the Investment Commission approval, including the mandatory Korea? no, including the periodic financial declarations, within thirty days, and retain all digital magazine platform agreements for regulatory inspection.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate
Tax registration application form
Company official seal and responsible person seal
Bank account activation form
Power of attorney or board resolution authorizing legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau delays issuance due to missing lease certificate, cure by presenting a new utility bill or lease registration. If bank activation is refused due to seal discrepancies, the board must issue a corrective resolution, re-carve the seal, and re-file. The secretary must then track a revised tax activation date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - Digital Magazine Publishing (ISIC 5813) is a pure digital/consulting activity and is not governed by Taiwan's industrial licensing boards for manufacturing, chemistry, assembly, or warehousing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no mandatory operating license exists for a digital magazine portal under Taiwanese law, beyond general business registration and tax registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) does not mandate EIA screening for digital publication activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the business is categorized as a software- and content-service entity with no physical industrial installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the digital magazine portal generates no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste; standard office refuse collection under municipal rules is the only environmental compliance obligation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for Civil Defense fire permits, structural load inspections, or industrial workplace clearances, as no physical plant, warehouse, or assembly facility is operated. If the company leases an office, it remains subject to standard local building fire-safety inspection requirements and Taiwan Occupational Safety and Health Administration compliance, but this requires no special industrial civil-defense certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan (R.O.C.) Ministry of Finance (MOF), Taxation Administration; online portals: 'Tax e-Filing and Payment Service' at tax.nat.gov.tw and 'E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform' at einvoice.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign enterprise supplying digital media services (e.g., magazine subscriptions or advertising placements) with annual sales to Taiwan customers exceeding NT$480,000 must register for Value-Added Business Tax with the Regional National Taxation Bureau. Procedure: (1) submit the Business Tax Registration Application (營業稅籍登記申請書), prepared in Mandarin; (2) appoint a tax representative who is a resident of Taiwan; (3) provide a certificate of incorporation issued by the home country; (4) submit a notarized power of attorney authorizing the tax representative; (5) receive the statutory Tax Identification Number (統一編號) assigned by the National Taxation Bureau. Since May 1, 2017, registration may be completed online via the MOF 'Tax Online Registration for Foreign E-commerce Operators' service, accessible through the tax.nat.gov.tw portal. The TIN remains permanently valid and must be cited on all Unified Invoices, electronic declarations, and cross-border remittance documents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Taiwan's Income Tax Act does not offer check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections. The CFC and PEM rules impose mandatory anti-deferral mechanisms applicable to foreign affiliates, and the Business Tax Act mandates the Uniform Invoice system without elective classification for VAT.)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Business Tax (VAT) under the Business Tax Act (加值型及非加值型營業稅)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a Taiwan-resident WFOE, business tax registration is mandatory upon incorporation regardless of turnover. For a foreign non-resident digital services provider, mandatory VAT registration is triggered when annual taxable sales to Taiwan customers exceed NT$480,000; below this threshold, the foreign entity may be subject to withholding tax at source on Taiwan-sourced revenue.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under Taiwan's Uniform Invoice Act and E-Invoice Implementation Regulations (電子發票作業要點), the WFOE must issue electronic Uniform Invoices through the MOF E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform or a certified turnkey device. Each e-invoice must be transmitted to the MOF E-Invoice Database within 48 hours of issuance. The platform mandates API-based real-time submission (Turnkey E-Invoice Transmission Solution), digital filing via the taxpayer's certificate, and compulsory issuance of Cloud Invoices (雲端發票) for qualifying digital sectors. Anti-fraud controls include sequential invoice numbering, encrypted QR codes generated by the platform, and automated cross-matching with the quarterly VAT e-Declaration System.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, zero-rating applies to exported goods and to services that are provided to foreign enterprises or individuals and are not deemed to be used inside Taiwan. For the digital magazine portal and sponsored media placements, zero-rating is claimable if the offshore customer (subscriber or advertiser) is located abroad, the intellectual commercial value is consumed overseas, and the WFOE retains written contracts, usage logs, and IP address evidence demonstrating overseas use. The company must be VAT-registered and must issue unified invoices in foreign currency where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration Form (出口報單) filed electronically via the MOF Trade Administration System - required when physical promotional materials or bundled print media cross the customs border
Bill of Lading (載貨證券) or Air Waybill (空運提單) - evidencing physical cross-border movement of exported goods, if any
Inward Remittance Certificate (外匯存入/結匯證明) or bank Foreign Exchange Receipt (外匯收入水單) - evidencing collection of export proceeds in foreign currency
Commercial contract, service invoice issued in foreign currency, and detailed usage report - substantiating the offshore supply and usability of digital services where no customs form applies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau conducts comprehensive audit scrutiny of export zero-rating claims. If documentary evidence is missing or the service is determined to have been used in Taiwan, the zero-rating is retrospectively revoked for up to five years, the underpaid 5% VAT is assessed, and a penalty of 1 to 5 times the underpaid tax (increasing to 5 to 10 times for cases of deliberate fraud) is imposed under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act. Fraudulent claims may also trigger criminal prosecution under Article 41 of the Tax Evasion and Penalty Act (稅捐稽徵法), carrying imprisonment up to 5 years. The enterprise bears the full burden of proof for overseas use and FX repatriation; failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days is prima facie evidence of a domestic sale.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC). The Taiwan jurisdiction identifier conflicts with the payload's China sovereign-country designation and WFOE entity label. Taiwan and mainland China have separate legal, banking, and foreign-exchange regimes; a mainland China WFOE cannot be treated as a Taiwan-incorporated entity. Confirm the entity's place of incorporation and operating jurisdiction before account opening or remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is generally convertible for current-account payments, subject to bank documentation, transaction reporting, sanctions screening, and applicable foreign-exchange settlement limits. Capital-account transactions, including inbound investment, capital reductions, dividends, intercompany lending, and disposal proceeds, are subject to Taiwan company, investment, tax, and foreign-exchange rules and may require filings, approvals, or supporting evidence. A Taiwan company generally needs distributable earnings, approved financial statements, tax clearance or evidence of tax payment, and corporate approvals to remit dividends. Mainland China remittances by a PRC WFOE instead fall under PRC foreign-exchange and cross-border payment rules; Taiwan rules do not govern that entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not generally impose a blanket mandatory conversion ratio or automatic surrender of ordinary export proceeds. Export receipts may generally be retained or converted through an authorized foreign-exchange bank, subject to applicable declarations, transaction documentation, settlement limits, and bank review. Banks may require export contracts, invoices, shipping or service evidence, and reconciliation of receipts. Confirm current CBC rules and the company's accumulated settlement position with the handling bank before material transactions. Do not apply this assessment to a mainland China WFOE, for which PRC rules may impose different registration, documentation, and settlement requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; foreign-currency account; capital or investment proceeds account if required by the approved Taiwan investment and banking structure

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a substitute for a Taiwan domestic corporate bank account. Offshore electronic-money institutions and payment platforms may support eligible collections or payouts only where the provider accepts the entity, country, business model, and settlement destination. They do not replace local banking, foreign-exchange documentation, investment registration, or regulatory reporting. Stripe and Google AdSense availability, contracting entity, settlement currencies, and payout eligibility must be confirmed against current Taiwan-specific provider terms. A mainland China WFOE may not use Taiwan availability as evidence of PRC eligibility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal statutory rule requires every director to appear in person for every Taiwan corporate account opening. The bank sets its own requirements and may require an in-person meeting, original documents, wet signatures, local representatives, or verified identity checks for authorized signatories, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners. Remote onboarding is bank- and risk-dependent and should not be assumed. A foreign-invested Taiwan entity must provide its valid registration and investment documentation. If the entity is a PRC WFOE, onboarding must be assessed under mainland China requirements instead.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch among the stated sovereign country (China), jurisdiction (Taiwan), and entity form (WFOE), or an application that presents a PRC entity as a Taiwan-incorporated company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide current certificate of incorporation or business registration, constitutional documents, registered-office evidence, ownership chart, ultimate-beneficial-owner declarations, foreign-investment approval or registration documents where applicable, tax registration, and a jurisdictional legal memorandum confirming the contracting entity and place of operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of capital, third-party funding, round-tripping concerns, or transfers between related mainland China and Taiwan parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide board and shareholder resolutions, subscription or capital-contribution agreements, investor identity and beneficial-ownership records, audited financial statements or source-of-funds evidence, bank statements showing the remitting account and ownership, intercompany agreements, and required investment, tax, and foreign-exchange filings or approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Digital publishing, sponsored placements, or advertising receipts that cannot be reconciled to customer contracts, platform statements, or declared business activities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed business description, website and content samples, advertising and sponsorship contracts, platform terms, invoices, campaign reports, payout statements, customer and advertiser profiles, refund policy, and transaction-level reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume or rapid pass-through flows, payments to unrelated third parties, unusual jurisdictions, or payment descriptions inconsistent with media-publishing revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a documented funds-flow map, expected monthly volumes and counterparties, underlying contracts and invoices, commercial rationale, payment approvals, sanctions-screening controls, and evidence that account use is limited to the stated business.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dividend, service-fee, royalty, loan, or capital remittances lacking a clear legal basis or tax and foreign-exchange support.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed intercompany agreements, transfer-pricing support where applicable, board approvals, financial statements, tax returns and payment evidence, withholding-tax analysis, distributable-profit calculation for dividends, and bank-required foreign-exchange declarations or approvals.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: First establish whether the recipient is a Taiwan company or a mainland China WFOE; do not route capital until the discrepancy is resolved. For a Taiwan recipient, use a regulated bank wire to the account and currency designated for the approved investment or capital contribution. Ensure the investor name matches the remitter, use an accurate capital-contribution or investment purpose description, and provide investment approvals or registrations, subscription documents, corporate resolutions, beneficial-ownership information, and source-of-funds evidence. The receiving bank applies CBC reporting and settlement rules and may request a foreign-exchange declaration and supporting documents. For a PRC WFOE, route only through its PRC bank under applicable foreign-investment registration, capital-account, and SAFE/PBOC requirements; Taiwan procedures and purpose descriptions are not substitutes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settle bona fide publisher, software, advertising, hosting, and other trade invoices by bank transfer, normally using SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wires and accurate beneficiary, invoice, currency, and payment-purpose data. Supply contracts, invoices, delivery or service evidence, and tax documentation requested by the bank. Use a documentary commercial letter of credit only where commercially appropriate and supported by the underlying transaction and bank facility. Reconcile platform payouts and customer receipts to contracts and invoices. Dividend, royalty, service-fee, loan, and capital-return payments are not trade disbursements and require separate legal, tax, corporate, and foreign-exchange review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward contracts with an authorized bank, subject to eligibility, underlying exposure evidence, bank credit approval, and applicable settlement and reporting rules.
Non-deliverable forwards only where offered by an authorized counterparty and permitted for the entity, exposure, and jurisdiction; confirm applicable product and settlement rules with the bank.
Currency swaps with an authorized financial institution, subject to documentation, credit approval, accounting treatment, and applicable regulatory reporting.

Do not hedge speculative positions or assume that a Taiwan product authorization applies to a mainland China WFOE; verify the entity's jurisdiction, permitted underlying exposure, and current bank requirements before execution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders meeting and approval of business report, financial statements, and profit distribution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; Ministry of Economic Affairs filing only where a registrable change results
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each fiscal year; normally by 30 June for a calendar-year company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Responsible directors may face administrative fines generally ranging from approximately TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000, with increased sanctions for repeated non-compliance; failure to register resulting corporate changes may trigger separate fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May following the close of the fiscal year for a calendar-year company; an approved extension may apply in prescribed circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur a surcharge generally equal to 10% of tax payable, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts; failure to file may result in tax assessment, higher penalties, interest, and collection enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding tax reconciliation and withholding statement reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Withholding statements are generally filed by 31 January following the calendar year; withholding tax remittances are generally due by the tenth day of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate reporting may result in penalties, interest, assessment of unpaid withholding tax, and joint liability of the withholding agent for amounts not properly withheld or remitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation and update of company registration particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent local authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Taiwan does not generally impose a universal annual return filing for ordinary private companies; amendments must generally be registered within 15 days after the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register changes within the statutory period may result in administrative fines generally ranging from approximately TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000 and may cause filing or banking restrictions until rectified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business tax and transaction reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Business tax is generally filed bimonthly by the 15th day of the following period; annual reconciliation is completed through the applicable periodic filings and annual income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment may trigger penalties, interest, tax assessment, and enforcement measures; non-filing may result in additional penalties and suspension or restriction of tax registration in serious cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit and certification may be mandatory for public companies and for companies meeting applicable Taiwan thresholds, including generally paid-in capital of at least TWD 30 million, annual net sales of at least TWD 100 million, total assets of at least TWD 100 million, or other prescribed regulatory criteria. Tax certification may also be required under separate tax rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards, substantially converged with IFRS, subject to company type, size, and applicable Taiwan accounting and tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not generally require a standalone annual UBO certification for every private company. The company must maintain accurate ownership and control information, update relevant corporate registrations after shareholding or control changes, and provide beneficial ownership information to competent authorities, financial institutions, and regulated professionals when required. Share transfers must be reflected in the shareholders register and reported where they create a registrable corporate change.

Accounting books and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-2,500 per year for registered office, company secretary, statutory correspondence, and routine compliance support; Taiwan does not generally require a separate registered agent in the common-law sense.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-12,000 per year for a small private foreign-invested company, depending on transaction volume, revenue, assets, foreign reporting requirements, and whether CPA tax certification is required.
